claims.text: The ROI section must keep three kinds of value distinct throughout: Hard-dollar: directly hits the P&L, such as cancelled tool licenses, avoided hires, or measurable ticket deflection. Soft-dollar: real but indirect, such as time saved, faster ramp, or improved satisfaction. Directional: hypothesis-grade, backed by benchmarks rather than customer data. Boundary A savings number without an implementation and measurement plan is incomplete. Never mix hard-dollar, soft-dollar, and directional benefits in one headline total.

claims.text: Glean's value-selling training makes a practical point about the mix of value in a business case. Cost reduction is easier to quantify, so it often anchors the hard-dollar case. claims.text: A defensible capacity model accounts for: Population: addressable users. Adoption: the share who actively use the capability. Frequency: events per active user per workday. Time: minutes per event, converted once to hours. Period: workdays per year. Removable share and coverage: how much of the burden Glean can realistically remove, and for what share of events. Recapture: the share of freed capacity that becomes useful business output. Loaded rate: the value of an hour, labeled as capacity value, not cash. Uncertainty: a risk adjustment.

claims.text: Glean's Value Playbook calls the productivity recapture rate the most consequential assumption in any value model. It answers this question: of the time Glean saves, how much actually converts into measurable business output? The honest answer is not all of it. claims.text: Net ROI = (benefit − cost) ÷ cost, with benefit and cost over the same period. Benefit/cost multiple = benefit ÷ cost. This is not net ROI. Simple payback (months) = cost ÷ (annual benefit ÷ 12). The ROI Lab uses this simplified form, which gives about 8.7 months in the base case. It is not a full cash-flow or NPV model. Say so before comparing it with a multi-year calculator. Include all the relevant costs: platform, implementation, adoption and enablement, and measurement.

claims.text: If the range is wide, the assumptions that drive it are where validation effort should go. Sensitivity is not a license to pick the most attractive result.
